ai_policy.summary: Journal adopts COPE guidance explicitly addressing AI use in manuscript writing, data collection and data analysis, and anticipates AI-produced manuscript content under human accountability. Explicit analysis supports the analysis/code category semantically; this is not a separate affirmative guarantee for every coding use.

disclosure.instructions: In Materials and Methods or a similar section identify the tool and explain how it was used for writing, graphical elements, or data collection and analysis.

restrictions: AI cannot be an author; authors are responsible for all content and must have permission for third-party content.

policy_sources.note: Journal adopts COPE language expressly addressing AI use in writing, data collection and analysis and human responsibility for AI-produced manuscript parts; disclosure is mandatory. Explicit analysis establishes the analysis/code category under the campaign contract.

findings.resolution: Mark analysis_code conditional and compatible using the contract semantic rule; preserve required disclosure and responsibility. Fees remain needs_verification.

findings.issue: Publisher policy describes study methodology and AI-generated code generally but also prohibits creation or manipulation of research data; it does not explicitly permit data analysis under that restriction.
findings.resolution: Retain unclear AI compatibility and fee uncertainty; do not infer analytical permission from disclosure or a generic definition of tools.

notes: Reviewed all eight merged candidates. IMS official AI policy ordinary direct HTTPS returned HTTP 200 bot challenge rather than the policy; web retrieval failed. Inaccessible evidence is not evidence of prohibition or permission.

No acceptance rates or additional official current metrics established in this review. Empty metric arrays reflect no verified figure, not absence of a metric. Geography distinguishes venue from publisher; no additional geography correction established.

Fee claims for the five IMS journals rest on search-rendered evidence; retain uncertainty until complete official submission and other mandatory charges are independently established. Lithuanian and Open Statistics fee limitations and Serbian submission-fee uncertainty remain.
